footerNote: Seeded defects are mutants. Mutation testing, inverted to grade the tests.

targets.checkout: Cart pricing: tiers, promos, shipping threshold, VAT.
targets.authn: Token issue and verification: expiry, signature, scope, revocation.
targets.ledger: Double-entry ledger: idempotency, invariants, pagination, currency.

defects.title: Promo percentage discounts shipping too
defects.description: The promo code percentage is applied to goods plus shipping instead of goods alone, so every discount code silently discounts delivery as well.
defects.hint: Price a cart below the free-shipping threshold with a promo code applied, and assert the promo discount equals the percentage of goods only. A cart that already qualifies for free shipping cannot see this defect.

defects.title: Quantity discount tier excludes its own boundary
defects.description: The tier test is qty > minimum rather than qty >= minimum, so a line of exactly 3, 6 or 12 units is charged at the tier below the one advertised.
defects.hint: Price lines at exactly 3, 6 and 12 units. Quantities either side of a boundary behave correctly, so only the boundary values themselves expose it.

defects.title: Total rounds half-to-even instead of half-up
defects.description: The single final quantize uses banker's rounding. Identical to the correct result on 99% of carts; one cent low on an exact half-cent tie.
defects.hint: Construct a cart whose pre-rounding total lands exactly on a half cent with an even preceding digit - 5 units at 1.41 gives 14.605 pre-VAT-rounding and is the cheapest such cart. Measured by brute force, only about 1% of single-line carts expose this at all.

defects.title: Free-shipping threshold is exclusive
defects.description: Free shipping tests goods > 50.00 instead of >= 50.00, so an order of exactly the advertised threshold is charged the delivery fee.
defects.hint: Price a cart whose goods total is exactly 50.00 and assert shipping is zero. 49.99 and 50.01 both behave correctly.

defects.title: VAT computed on the pre-discount subtotal
defects.description: Tax is calculated from goods plus shipping, ignoring the promo discount, so every discounted order is overcharged VAT on money the customer never paid.
defects.hint: Price the same cart with and without a promo code and assert the VAT falls in proportion. Checking only the discount line, or only an undiscounted cart, misses it entirely.

defects.title: Non-positive quantity validation dropped
defects.description: The guard rejecting qty <= 0 is gone. A negative line quantity is accepted and becomes a silent credit against the order total.
defects.hint: Assert that a cart line with qty 0 or -1 raises ValueError. Any suite that only feeds valid carts cannot see a missing validation guard.

defects.title: Expired tokens accepted inside a one-hour grace window
defects.description: A 3600-second leeway was added 'for clock skew'. Tokens keep verifying for a full hour after they expire.
defects.hint: Verify a token at exactly one second past expiry. Probing far past expiry - the obvious way to write an expiry test - still gets rejected, so the defect hides from anyone who does not test at the edge.

defects.title: Signature compared on its first 8 characters only
defects.description: The HMAC comparison is truncated to 8 hex characters, reducing a 256-bit signature to 32 bits of real protection.
defects.hint: Tamper with the tail of a valid signature and assert verification fails. Replacing the whole signature with garbage is still rejected, so the standard 'a bad signature is refused' assertion passes.

defects.title: Substring role test bypasses the scope check
defects.description: The admin bypass matches any role containing 'admin', so roles such as billing_admin or admin_readonly skip scope authorisation entirely.
defects.hint: Issue a token whose role merely contains the substring 'admin' and no scopes, then demand a privileged scope. Testing the literal roles 'admin' and 'user' shows correct behaviour in both directions.

defects.title: Malformed token returns None instead of raising
defects.description: The documented contract is claims-or-AuthError. A malformed token now returns None, so callers that bind the result carry a None identity into the session.
defects.hint: Assert that garbage input raises AuthError specifically, not merely that it is falsy. assert not verify_token(...) passes against this defect.

defects.title: Revocation matched against subject instead of token id
defects.description: The revocation list holds token ids but is checked against the subject claim, so revoking a token has no effect at all.
defects.hint: Issue a token, revoke it by its jti, then verify it again and expect rejection. Requires carrying state between two calls; a single-call test cannot see it.

defects.title: Signature verification sampled by a load-shedding fast path
defects.description: A performance 'fast path' skips signature verification on roughly 30% of calls. A forged token is therefore accepted intermittently rather than never.
defects.hint: Verify a forged token repeatedly rather than once. A single probe catches this about 30% of the time, so a suite that asserts it once is itself flaky - which is what the flake-rate column measures.

defects.title: Idempotency guard narrowed to zero-amount entries
defects.description: The dedupe guard now only fires when the entry amount is zero, so any real retry of a payment posts a second time and the ledger double-counts.
defects.hint: Post the identical entry twice with the same idempotency key and assert the ledger holds one row. A suite that posts each fixture once cannot see it.

defects.title: Double-entry invariant skipped for small entries
defects.description: Entries whose largest leg is under 10.00 bypass the balance check, so unbalanced small entries are accepted and corrupt every downstream balance.
defects.hint: Post a deliberately unbalanced entry under 10.00 and assert it is refused. An unbalanced entry over the threshold is still correctly refused.

defects.title: Page offset off by one after the first page
defects.description: Pages after the first start one row early, so every page boundary repeats the previous page's last row and a paged export double-counts.
defects.hint: Read two adjacent pages and assert their ids are disjoint and contiguous. Reading page 1 alone, or checking only page length, shows nothing wrong.

defects.title: Account balance sums across currencies
defects.description: The currency filter is ignored, so EUR and USD legs are added together as if the rate were 1.0 and the reported balance is meaningless.
defects.hint: Seed one account with entries in two currencies, then ask for the balance in one of them. A single-currency ledger cannot expose this.

defects.title: Tenant filter dropped on the unfiltered listing
defects.description: When no account filter is supplied the tenant filter is skipped entirely, so the default listing returns every tenant's entries.
defects.hint: List entries for one tenant with no other filter, in a store holding more than one tenant, and assert every row belongs to the caller. Listing with an account filter applies the tenant filter correctly.

suites.name: Expert
suites.blurb: Careful human-style checks: exact expected values, both sides of every boundary, stateful sequences, and a few invariant assertions.
suites.expectation: Reference ceiling. Everything else is measured against this.
suites.method: Hand-written against the target source with the defect catalog hidden.
suites.caveat: Written by the same author as the targets, which is a real bias: the ceiling is 'what this author thought to probe', not 'what is findable'.

suites.name: Spec checklist
suites.blurb: Shallow happy-path checks read straight off the spec. Loose assertions - 'the total is positive', 'the discount reduces it' - and no exact values.
suites.expectation: The control. This is what a suite looks like when it only looks like a suite.
suites.method: Transcribed from the written spec bullet by bullet, without reading the code.
suites.caveat: Deliberately shallow. Included as a floor, not as a straw man to beat.

suites.name: LLM, spec only
suites.blurb: Recorded output for the spec-only condition: plausible coverage, some redundancy, subtle paths missed, and two checks that assert behaviour the spec does not actually promise.
suites.expectation: Reads as competent. The false positives are the interesting part.
suites.method: Authored once as a fixture representing the spec-only condition: written from the prose specification with no access to the target source and no ability to run anything.
suites.caveat: Committed fixture. This suite is a Python file in this repository, authored once and checked in. Buggy does not call any model at run time, needs no API key, and never regenerates a suite live. Live generation is an unbuilt future phase.

suites.name: LLM, code and tools
suites.blurb: Recorded output for the code-reading condition: exact expected values, real boundary probes, stateful sequences. Still blind to three defects the expert suite finds.
suites.expectation: The honest question: how much of the gap does tool access actually close?
suites.method: Authored once as a fixture representing the code-reading condition: written with the target source visible and the freedom to execute it while drafting.
suites.caveat: Committed fixture. This suite is a Python file in this repository, authored once and checked in. Buggy does not call any model at run time, needs no API key, and never regenerates a suite live. Live generation is an unbuilt future phase.

expertChecks.title: Plain cart prices to the exact expected total
expertChecks.intent: Anchor the whole pricing pipeline on one exact value.

expertChecks.title: Quantity tier includes its lower boundary (qty 3)
expertChecks.intent: A tier advertised as 'from 3' must apply at exactly 3.

expertChecks.title: Quantity tiers include their boundaries at 6 and 12
expertChecks.intent: The same off-by-one can be seeded at any tier, so probe all of them.

expertChecks.title: Free shipping applies at exactly the threshold
expertChecks.intent: 'Free over 50' has to mean free AT 50; this is the classic inclusive-bound bug.

expertChecks.title: Shipping is charged just below and free just above the threshold
expertChecks.intent: Pin the other side of the boundary so a fix cannot overshoot.

expertChecks.title: Promo percentage applies to goods, never to shipping
expertChecks.intent: A discount code must not quietly discount delivery.

expertChecks.title: VAT falls when a promo is applied
expertChecks.intent: Tax is owed on what was actually charged, not on the pre-discount subtotal.

expertChecks.title: Non-positive quantities are rejected
expertChecks.intent: A missing validation guard is invisible unless something invalid is sent.

expertChecks.title: Invariant: goods equals the sum of line nets
expertChecks.intent: Structural invariant that must hold for every cart, defect or not.

expertChecks.title: An unknown promo code is a no-op
expertChecks.intent: Unrecognised codes must not error and must not discount.

expertChecks.title: Issue and verify round-trips the claims
expertChecks.intent: Baseline: the happy path works and the claims survive.

expertChecks.title: A token is rejected one second past expiry
expertChecks.intent: Expiry must bite at the edge; probing far past expiry proves nothing.

expertChecks.title: A token is still valid at exactly its expiry second
expertChecks.intent: Pin the inclusive side of the expiry bound so a fix cannot overshoot.

expertChecks.title: A signature tampered only in its tail is rejected
expertChecks.intent: A truncated comparison passes garbage-signature tests but fails this one.

expertChecks.title: A privilege forgery is rejected on every one of 12 attempts
expertChecks.intent: Repeat the probe: an intermittently-skipped check is invisible to a single attempt.

expertChecks.title: A role merely containing 'admin' does not bypass scopes
expertChecks.intent: Substring role matching is the classic silent authorisation hole.

expertChecks.title: A malformed token raises AuthError, not a falsy return
expertChecks.intent: The contract is claims-or-raise; a None return breaks every caller that binds it.

expertChecks.title: Revoking a token by its id stops it verifying
expertChecks.intent: Needs two calls with state between them; a single-call test cannot see it.

expertChecks.title: Replaying an idempotency key posts exactly once
expertChecks.intent: The retry is the test; posting each fixture once can never see a broken key.

expertChecks.title: A small unbalanced entry is refused
expertChecks.intent: Invariants get bypassed for 'cheap' rows; probe under the cheap threshold.

expertChecks.title: A large unbalanced entry is refused
expertChecks.intent: The other side of the size threshold, so a fix cannot pass by narrowing it.

expertChecks.title: Adjacent pages are disjoint and contiguous
expertChecks.intent: A page-edge defect is only visible when two pages are compared to each other.

expertChecks.title: An account balance is scoped to one currency
expertChecks.intent: Mixed-currency ledgers are where a missing filter becomes a wrong number.

expertChecks.title: An unfiltered listing is still scoped to the caller's tenant
expertChecks.intent: Tenant leaks hide on the default path, which is the path nobody filters.
